title: Feedzai Competitors: 8 Fraud Platforms Compared
summary: Feedzai competitors compared: Featurespace, FICO Falcon, NICE Actimize, BioCatch and more, with ownership changes and where Sphinx fits after the alert.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** The main Feedzai competitors are enterprise fraud suites (Featurespace, FICO Falcon, NICE Actimize, SAS, ACI), newer platforms that span fraud and AML (Hawk, Sardine), and the behavioral layer BioCatch. Ownership is the live story: Visa owns Featurespace and has agreed to buy BioCatch, and NICE is reported to be in talks to sell Actimize. Reported consumer fraud losses reached about $16 billion in 2025, according to the FTC, which is why scoring choices get revisited.


Sphinx wrote this list, using vendor material, filings and press, and the numbers are an order of fit for a team replacing Feedzai's real-time fraud scoring, not a quality ranking.


Sphinx is not on the numbered list. It does not score transactions in real time, so it is not a Feedzai competitor in the sense most buyers mean.


## What Feedzai does, and why teams compare it anyway


Feedzai is a RiskOps platform that scores payments and customer events for fraud and supports AML work on the same system. The company says it risk-assesses $19 trillion in payments a year across 140 billion events. In the past 18 months it has announced RiskFM, a foundation model trained on financial data, added transaction screening through a partnership with Neterium, and launched Farol, an AI agent embedded in its analyst workflow. It raised about $75 million at a valuation above $2 billion in October 2025 and remains independent, and it reported being first-ranked tenderer in a European Central Bank framework agreement for digital euro fraud prevention.


None of that suggests a product in trouble. Teams search for Feedzai alternatives for more ordinary reasons. A contract is up for renewal and procurement wants a real comparison. A card-heavy issuer wants to weigh consortium models against behavioral ones. A smaller institution wants a lighter deployment. A bank on one vendor's payments stack wants fraud from the same place. Fraud pressure adds to this: the[FTC reported about $16 billion in consumer fraud losses for 2025](https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2026/06/ftc-data-show-people-reported-losing-3-point-5-billion-imposter-scams-2025) , the highest on record and about 25% above 2024. Our[wider comparison of fraud detection platforms](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/best-fraud-detection-platforms) covers the category beyond this one vendor.


## Featurespace vs Feedzai: where the real difference sits


Featurespace vs Feedzai is mostly a question of model philosophy and ownership. Featurespace built its name on Adaptive Behavioral Analytics, which profiles each customer's genuine behavior and flags departures from it. Feedzai now describes itself around a broader lifecycle, from onboarding through payments and AML, and around pooled intelligence delivered through its own models and scores.


The ownership gap is plainer.[Visa completed its purchase of Featurespace in December 2024](https://www.pymnts.com/partnerships/2024/visa-finalizes-featurespace-purchase-boost-fraud-prevention/) , and the business sits in Visa's Risk and Identity Solutions unit. Feedzai is an independent company. Some buyers will read a network owner as reach and distribution. Others will prefer a vendor with no card network above it. Both are reasonable positions, and neither says anything about detection quality, which only a test on your own data can settle.


## The eight options at a glance


Vendor Best for What it is Ownership


Featurespace Behavioral scoring across payment types Real-time fraud and transaction monitoring platform Visa, since December 2024


FICO Falcon Fraud Manager Card issuers wanting consortium models Transaction fraud scoring with case management FICO, publicly listed


NICE Actimize Large banks wanting a broad fraud suite Enterprise fraud management platform NICE, sale talks reported


SAS Fraud Decisioning Institutions already invested in SAS Cloud-native fraud decisioning on SAS Viya SAS, private


ACI Fraud Management Banks running ACI payments Fraud management and scoring tied to a payments platform ACI Worldwide, publicly listed


Hawk Mid-market to large banks wanting fraud, AML and screening together Modular financial crime platform Private, venture-backed


Sardine Fintechs and banks on instant payment rails Fraud, AML and monitoring platform Private, venture-backed


BioCatch Adding behavioral signals to an existing engine Behavioral and device intelligence layer Sale to Visa agreed, not yet closed


## The list, in order of fit


Entries near the top are closer like-for-like replacements for Feedzai's scoring. Entries lower down cover part of the job, or suit a narrower buyer.


### 1. Featurespace — Best for behavioral scoring across payment types


Featurespace, now sold as a Visa solution, monitors customer activity in real time using Adaptive Behavioral Analytics and Automated Deep Behavioral Networks. Its platform, including ARIC Risk Hub, covers card, payment, application and merchant acquiring fraud, plus financial crime detection, and feeds analyst decisions back into its models. Visa says its enhanced A2A Protect, launched in September 2026, carries a unified fraud score and is the first in-market integration of Featurespace technology. It suits institutions that want the closest functional match to Feedzai and like a customer-behavior approach. The honest limit comes from the ownership: the roadmap now sits inside a card network, so buyers with heavy non-Visa volumes should ask how product priorities are set.


### 2. FICO Falcon Fraud Manager — Best for card issuers wanting consortium models


FICO Falcon Fraud Manager scores transactions for fraud risk, with a direct link to authorization systems so a payment can be declined at the point of sale. FICO says Falcon protects more than 4 billion payment cards, and that its models train on tagged transactions from a consortium of more than 10,000 financial institutions. FICO has since added scam detection models and a wider Enterprise Fraud Solution on FICO Platform. It suits issuers and processors that value a long-running card model and shared data. The limit follows from how consortium models work: they learn from pooled history, so a portfolio that looks unlike the pool should test performance on its own data before relying on the score.


### 3. NICE Actimize — Best for large banks wanting a broad fraud suite


NICE Actimize's IFM platform covers payments fraud, scams and mule activity, new account fraud, authentication and investigations, with a separate Xceed offering for small and mid-sized banks. It suits large institutions that want many fraud use cases and their investigation tooling from one vendor. Ownership is the open question.[CTech, citing Sky News, reported in September 2026](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/iazqvedg2) that Brookfield was in exclusive talks to buy Actimize from NICE for about $2 billion, and cautioned that the deal could still fall apart. We found no announced agreement as of late October. The limit for a new buyer is that uncertainty, so ask about change-of-control terms and roadmap commitments before signing a multi-year contract.


### 4. SAS Fraud Decisioning — Best for institutions already invested in SAS


SAS Fraud Decisioning is a cloud-native product on SAS Viya covering payment, account takeover, application, synthetic identity, check and digital fraud. It includes prebuilt models, model governance, alert triage and case management, and SAS supports a combined fraud and AML approach across its financial crime products. SAS remains private, held by its two co-founders. It suits institutions with analytics teams that want control over models and already work in the SAS environment. The limit comes from the architecture: adopting the product means adopting SAS Viya, which is a larger decision for a team that only wants a fraud score through an API.


### 5. ACI Fraud Management — Best for banks running ACI payments


ACI Worldwide sells fraud management for financial institutions as a service, in public cloud or on premises, using what it calls incremental machine learning. ACI Fraud Scoring Services delivers a score with an explanation through API calls, and is designed to complement existing fraud tools. ACI Connetic, its cloud-native platform, brings account-to-account payments, card payments and fraud prevention onto one architecture. It suits banks that already process payments on ACI or are considering it. The limit is the flip side of that pitch: a bank on another payments stack gets less from the unified architecture and should judge the fraud product on its own.


### 6. Hawk — Best for fraud, AML and screening in one contract


Hawk offers modular AML, screening and fraud products on one platform, with real-time fraud decisions it puts at 150 milliseconds on average, self-serve rule management and check fraud coverage. It also lists investigative and screening agents. The company raised a $56 million Series C in April 2025 and reported more than 80 customers at the time, from large banks to fintechs. It suits institutions consolidating fraud and AML vendors. The limit is scale of evidence: that customer count is a smaller reference pool than older vendors on this list, so ask for references that match your size and payment mix.


### 7. Sardine — Best for fintechs and banks on instant payment rails


Sardine positions itself as a risk platform unifying fraud prevention, AML and transaction monitoring for banks, merchants and fintechs. It evaluates payments before funds move across ACH, wires, SEPA, RTP, FedNow, Zelle and checks, using behavioral, device and network signals, and it offers Sardine Flow for building workflows that connect data, rules and AI agents. It suits digital-first institutions where payments are irreversible within seconds. The limit comes from its breadth: much of the value assumes consolidation, so a large bank locked into separate fraud and AML contracts may only be able to use part of it at first.


### 8. BioCatch — Best for adding behavioral signals to an existing engine


BioCatch analyzes application, behavioral, device and network signals, such as keystrokes and touch gestures, to separate real users from fraudsters and coerced customers during a digital session. Products cover account opening, account takeover, mule accounts and scams.[CNBC reported in August 2026](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/03/visa-buys-biocatch-fraud-detection.html) that Visa will buy it for $2.4 billion in cash from Permira and other investors, with closing expected by the end of Visa's fiscal second quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals. If it closes, Visa will own two names on this list. BioCatch comes last because it is more often an addition than a substitute. Its signals come from digital sessions, and it describes itself as working alongside existing controls, so it does not replace a transaction decisioning engine on its own.


## Where Sphinx fits: after the alert


Sphinx works on the investigation that follows a fraud or AML alert, whichever system raised it. Every platform above produces alerts, and someone still has to pull the transaction history, check the counterparties, run the KYC or KYB checks, write the case note and reach a view. Sphinx's AI analysts log into the tools a team already uses, prepare the evidence, apply your SOPs and produce a traceable recommendation. Your team retains final approval.


That makes Sphinx an addition, not a replacement. It will not block a payment or generate a score, so a team that needs real-time decisioning needs one of the vendors above. For teams already on Actimize, Hawk or Sardine, the useful question may be whether to replace the tool or add an investigation layer on top. Several of these vendors are building investigation agents of their own, so compare what each does in your workflow. The Sphinx median case takes 3.2 minutes, with 94-98% agreement with analysts, and[Sphinx's AI agents](https://sphinxhq.com/products/ai-agents) took Alviere from 14 to 2.4 minutes per case. Teams merging the two functions may also want our explainer on[FRAML and fraud-AML convergence](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/what-is-framl-fraud-aml-convergence) .


## How to choose without a vendor in the room


Start with where the loss or the workload actually sits. A team losing money to scams on instant rails has a different problem from one with a[false alert queue](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/reduce-false-alerts-transaction-monitoring) it cannot clear, and a new scoring engine only addresses the first. If you are replacing a scoring engine, these questions separate the options quickly:


- Which payment types carry most of your fraud losses, and does the vendor show results on those rails specifically?
- Will the vendor run a back-test on your own historical data, measured at your actual review rate?
- Who owns the vendor today, who may own it at renewal, and what does your contract say about a change of control?
- Does scoring run in line with authorization, and what happens to payments if the service is slow? Our piece on[how banks detect fraud in real time](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/how-banks-detect-fraudulent-transactions-real-time) covers why this matters.
- What does an analyst receive with an alert, and who does the investigation work once it fires?


Scoring gets the attention in a vendor evaluation, but the second half of the process is where the review hours go. A bank's SAR deadline, under FinCEN's rule, is generally 30 calendar days from initial detection of facts that may support a filing, and no detection engine files that report for you.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Who are Feedzai's main competitors?


The closest competitors for real-time fraud scoring are Featurespace, FICO Falcon Fraud Manager, NICE Actimize, SAS Fraud Decisioning and ACI Fraud Management. Hawk and Sardine compete with platforms that span fraud and AML. BioCatch overlaps on scams and account takeover, though it usually sits alongside a decisioning engine.


### Does Visa own Featurespace and BioCatch?


Visa completed its acquisition of Featurespace in December 2024. It signed a definitive agreement to buy BioCatch for $2.4 billion in August 2026, and that deal remains subject to regulatory approvals, with closing expected by the end of Visa's fiscal second quarter of 2027.


### Is NICE Actimize being sold?


Press reports say NICE has been running a sale process, and Sky News reported in September 2026 that Brookfield was in exclusive talks at about $2 billion. Neither company had announced a signed deal as of late October 2026, so treat the buyer and price as unconfirmed.


### Is Sphinx a Feedzai alternative?


No. Sphinx does not score transactions in real time or decide whether a payment clears. It handles the investigation work after a fraud or AML alert, and it runs alongside a detection platform. Pricing is a platform fee plus usage tiers scoped to your volumes.


### Do Feedzai competitors publish pricing?


We found no public rate card on the vendor pages we read for this list. Featurespace's AWS Marketplace listing says standard pricing is per transaction, with custom pricing by private offer. Expect pricing to depend on volumes and scope, and get it in writing during the evaluation.
